diagnostic_evidence.quote: Further, let $(\bar{\rho},\bar{c})$ with $\bar{\rho} \in C(0,T;H^1)$, $\partial_t \bar{\rho} \in C(0,T;H^{-1})$ and $\bar{c} \in C(0,T;H^2)$ be a solution to the perturbed system
We combine the stability frameworks in Theorem~\ref{stab_thm} and  Theorem~\ref{stab_cont} with the \emph{a posteriori} residual estimate (\ref{estimator}) to obtain $i)$ and $ii)$, respectively.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorems stab_thm and stab_cont are derived within the standing framework of Section 3, which assumes $\bar\rho\in C(0,T;H^1)$, $\partial_t\bar\rho\in C(0,T;H^{-1})$, $\bar c\in C(0,T;H^2)$ and that $(\bar\rho,\bar c)$ solves the perturbed system (res_bdrKS). The reconstruction actually used, $\tilde\rho(t)=\ell_0^n(t)\tilde\rho^{n+1}+\ell_1^n(t)\tilde\rho^n$, has a piecewise-constant time derivative that is discontinuous at the time nodes, so it fails $\partial_t\bar\rho\in C(0,T;H^{-1})$. Moreover cor:added-1 hypothesizes only $\tilde\rho\in L^\infty(0,T;L^2)\cap L^2(0,T;H^1)$ and nothing about $\tilde c$'s elliptic consistency or the perturbed-system structure. Hence the energy estimate (energy_esti), the foundation of both frameworks, is invoked in cor:added-1 (and likewise cor:added-2 and main_thm) without its hypotheses being established.

failure_location.quote: Let $\tilde{\rho} \in L^\infty(0,T;L^2) \cap L^2(0,T;H^1)$ be a reconstruction of a numerical approximation to $\rho$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the framework's assumption to $\partial_t\bar\rho\in L^2(0,T;H^{-1})$ (satisfied by the reconstruction) and justify (energy_esti) in integrated/a.e. form via a standard time-mollification argument; correspondingly state the actual regularity and elliptic consistency of the reconstruction in cor:added-1, cor:added-2 and main_thm.
issues.overall_effect: The derivations of cor:added-1, cor:added-2 and of the error bounds in main_thm i)/ii) rest on an energy estimate that is not justified, under the stated hypotheses, for the reconstruction to which it is applied.
issues.title: Stability framework invoked outside its regularity hypotheses (reconstruction time derivative is discontinuous)
issues.why_classification: The repair is a routine local weakening plus a standard justification step; all statements, conditions, quantities and advertised rates survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The continuation argument yields only per-interval bounds $\sup_{[t^n,t^{n+1}]}\|e\|^2+\int_{t^n}^{t^{n+1}}|e|^2\leq\Psi_n$. Therefore $\sup_{[0,T]}\|e\|^2\leq\max_n\Psi_n=\Psi_{N_t-1}$ (as $\Psi_n$ is increasing), but $\int_0^T|e|_{H^1}^2dt\leq\sum_{n=0}^{N_t-1}\Psi_n$, and $\sum_n\Psi_n$ is not bounded by $\Psi_{N_t-1}$: since $\delta_n>1$ and $E_n\geq e^{\Delta t^n/4}$ can both be arbitrarily close to $1$ (small time steps, small residuals), the $\Psi_n$ can be nearly constant, giving $\sum_n\Psi_n\approx N_t\Psi_{N_t-1}$. The final assembly step 'we obtain ... $\leq\Psi_{N_t-1}$' is an invalid inference; only the sup-part of the stated bound is proved.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the conclusion as $\sup_{[0,T]}\|e\|^2+\int_0^T|e|^2\leq\max_n\Psi_n+\sum_{n=0}^{N_t-1}\Psi_n$ (e.g. $\leq(N_t+1)\Psi_{N_t-1}$) and adjust the bound in main_thm ii) accordingly; per-step quantities and convergence orders in $h$ are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative conclusion of Theorem stab_cont and of estimator ii) in Theorem main_thm is unreliable: the $L^2(0,T;H^1)$-part of the bound can be underestimated by a factor of order $N_t$. The sup-part, the root conditions, and the a posteriori existence conclusions (cor:added-2 and the existence clause of main_thm ii)) remain valid.
issues.title: Global bound $\Psi_{N_t-1}$ in the local-in-time continuation theorem is not established by the per-interval estimates
issues.why_classification: A contained weakening (a factor at most $N_t+1$ in one component of the bound) preserves the framework, conditions, existence conclusions and rates, but the theorem's stated guarantee itself must be weakened; no local edit proves the stated bound.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper's standing initial-data class is $\rho_0\in L^2(\Omega)$ (Section 2 and the hypotheses of apostverif, cor:added-1/2, main_thm). $L^2$ functions are equivalence classes defined up to null sets and have no well-defined point values, so sampling $\rho_0$ at the circumcenters $x_K$ is not well defined: changing $\rho_0$ on the null set $\{x_K\}$ changes the algorithm's output. The same sampling is repeated in the reconstruction of $\tilde\rho^0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims the experiments compute the error estimator (estimator) using Algorithm FV-FE. However, both tests are built on manufactured solutions of systems with nonzero source terms $f$ (in the evolution equation) and $g$ (in the elliptic equation), and the 3D test uses mixed periodic/Neumann boundary conditions, whereas the schemes (FV)/(FE), the Morley reconstruction, the residual $R_{\tilde\rho}$ and all residual lemmas are defined and derived only for the source-free, purely Neumann system (the mixed-BC case is covered only by a Remark asserting 'equal applicability' without proof). The paper never specifies how $f$, $g$ or the changed boundary conditions enter the scheme, the reconstruction or the estimator. Hence the quantities computed in the experiments are not the defined estimator/algorithm, and the experimental claims do not refer to the objects the paper defines and analyzes.

failure_location.quote: In this numerical test, we examine the order of convergence of the error estimator (\ref{estimator}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the source-adapted (and mixed-BC) variants of the scheme, reconstruction, residual and estimator -- including the required data-oscillation terms for $f$ and $g$ and boundary modifications -- and verify the residual analysis extends; or restrict the experimental claims to the analyzed setting.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical validation of the central a posteriori estimator -- its observed linear convergence and the availability comparison of the two estimators in Table stab_comp and Table scaling -- is performed in a setting not covered by any definition or analysis in the paper, so these experimental claims are unsupported as stated.
issues.title: Numerical experiments performed on sourced / mixed-boundary problems outside the defined and analyzed scheme and estimator
issues.why_classification: The repair requires a systematic (though mechanical) extension of the scheme, the residual identity and the residual estimates, or a substantive weakening of the numerical claims; it is contained and avoids major loss, but is not a short local edit.
